experiment: T7 Level-2: Does S2 survive aggregation? (RECALC with model comparison)
verdict: REFUTED — S2 is NOT an emergent fixed point of aggregation
methodological_correction: Original R²=0.997 was misleading. R² inflates for monotonic decay curves. AICc model comparison is the correct metric.

N_5000_broad_distribution.interpretation: S2_DUST beats S2 by ΔAICc=744. The aggregate is definitively NOT closed under single S2. It is better described as a two-component mixture.

residual_analysis.interpretation: Systematic deviation at small λ. The mixture is dominated by fast-decaying components at small λ, then slow ones at large λ. Single S2 cannot capture this two-regime structure.

why_R2_was_misleading: Any smooth monotonic function from 1 to 0 will fit R² > 0.99 against any other smooth monotonic function from 1 to 0. R² is not a meaningful metric for decay curves. AICc (which penalizes parameter count) is the correct metric for model comparison.
honest_conclusion: The three-level hierarchy collapses to two: Level 0 (local S2, confirmed) and Level 1 (interference, confirmed — mixtures do NOT simplify back to single S2). Level 2 (emergence) is refuted: aggregates of local S2s do not converge back to a single S2. They remain mixtures, better described by S2_DUST or BIEXP.
what_this_means_for_T7: T7 (interference) is the right picture. The aggregate is a mixture, not an emergent single S2. The original claim that S2 is an emergent fixed point of aggregation was wrong — it was an artifact of using R² instead of AICc.
